attacks.claim: Share links embed the owner's real project API key in the URL query string, and the share page returns it to any viewer as replayKey. The key leaks through browser history, referrers, logs, and Open Graph/Slack/X unfurl crawlers. Deleting a share only removes the record (404) and does not revoke or rotate the key, so the exposure is permanent.
attacks.evidence: url.searchParams.set("k", project.apiKey); ... replayKey: url.searchParams.get("k"); "Shares can be deleted from Playground → History; deleted shares return 404." ABSENT: key rotation or revocation on share delete.

attacks.claim: Anyone with a share link can re-run it against the owner's project quota and pro billing without authenticating. There is no per-link limit, no disclosure to the owner, and no revocation path, so strangers can spend the owner's paid tokens.
attacks.evidence: "Anyone with the link can view the conversation and re-run it, even without a Lumen account." and "// Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota."

attacks.claim: The $4k/month free-tier budget has no enforced spend cap. The free pool can autoscale to max_replicas 24 of H100s (about $43k/month at $2.49/h), signups are email-only with no card, and the only alert fires at more than 6 replicas. The rollback flag stops new signups but leaves existing free keys working, so an abuse wave keeps driving GPU spend.
attacks.evidence: free-8b: min_replicas: 2, max_replicas: 24, scale_on: queue_depth > 8 for 60s; "Free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call"; "`free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working." ABSENT: spend cap, spend alert, or throttle for existing free keys.

attacks.claim: The advertised 100k tokens/day free limit has no config behind it. The free block sets max_tokens_per_request and rate limits but no daily_tokens key, while pro explicitly sets daily_tokens: null. The public promise is therefore not enforced by the shipped config.
attacks.evidence: free: models: [...], rate_limit: {...}, max_tokens_per_request: 4096, pool: free-8b vs "Free accounts get 20 requests per minute and 100k tokens per day"

attacks.claim: The shipped free rate limit is 20 requests per second with burst 40, which is about 60x the advertised 20 requests per minute. The 429/Retry-After QA passed only against a staging config using per: minute, so the production config was never tested.
attacks.evidence: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } vs "Free accounts get **20 requests per minute**"; QA: "(staging config used `per: minute`)"

attacks.claim: Capacity sizing uses steady-state averages and does not model the HN/X launch spike, peak-to-average ratio, or per-key concurrency. The 2-replica minimum and the under-30% utilization claim are therefore unsupported for launch-day load.
attacks.evidence: "3,000 free DAU in month 1, avg 35 requests/day each, ~1.2k tokens per request" and "Launch post: Wed 17:00 UTC (blog, HN, X)"

attacks.claim: Shares snapshot the full session message history and are publicly viewable by anyone with the link. There is no consent prompt, expiry, noindex, or retention period for db.shares or the snapshotted messages, and Open Graph unfurling pushes the content to third parties. Users may share sensitive prompts or third-party personal data.
attacks.evidence: messages: session.messages, ... "Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X." ABSENT: share retention, expiry, or consent step.

attacks.claim: The share ID is the only access control on shared content, and the proposal does not state its entropy or whether IDs are unguessable. The share lookup also has no owner or visibility check, so sequential or guessable IDs would enable enumeration.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: share ID generation scheme; db.shares.get(params.id) with no owner check

attacks.claim: The claim that free traffic cannot degrade paid latency has no supporting test in the QA summary. Isolation is asserted by pool separation alone, with no pro-latency test under free load.
attacks.evidence: "Free pool is isolated from `shared-h100`, so free traffic cannot degrade paid latency." ABSENT: pro-latency test under free load in QA summary.

attacks.claim: There is no production monitoring of free-tier daily token totals or of spend. The /v1/usage reconciliation passed only in staging, and the alerts cover replica count and error rate, not cost.
attacks.evidence: "/v1/usage matches billing ledger within 0.1%: pass." and "Alerting: free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call; error rate > 2% pages on-call."

attacks.claim: The rollout has an unexplained gap. Gateway and models deploy at 16:00 UTC, signups open at 16:45 UTC, and the launch post goes out at 17:00 UTC, with no stated reason for the intervals or a check before the public post.
attacks.evidence: "Deploy gateway config and playground at 16:00 UTC, flag `free_signup_open` on at 16:45 UTC." Launch post: "Wed 17:00 UTC"
